assumptions: One immutable platform terminal-event receipt, two invocation tokens and at most two claims; primary clock0..5 and source/projection revisions1..3.
Provider object validation and complete matching reconciliation evidence are abstract predicates, not a proof of Stripe authenticity, freshness, field-level validation or financial terms.

Tentative publication becomes visible only when the final live-lease CAS commits. The receipt row remains locked during the transaction, so another claimant waits; expiry may still occur while the lock is held.
The terminal reconciliation acknowledgement requires matching current immutable source and derived projection; historical receipt replay does not imply that its old source remains current.

The commit action abstracts the final lease-guarded SQL write and successful atomic transaction under row locks. appliedAt is that decision clock, not a bound on COMMIT or HTTP acknowledgement time; storage and transport may finish later.
bounds.progress: No fairness, liveness or real-time bound is claimed.
bounds.conformance: All47 named PGlite cases must execute and pass without skips.

limitations: Provider payload validation and complete matching reconciliation evidence are abstractions, not proofs of provider authenticity or all field-level validators.
Generic applyEvent/reconcileEvent/listStuckEvents have no live subscription production call sites in the audited cloud tree; they are excluded from the transactional-publication guarantee.
Failed/quarantined administrative recovery and app-scoped receipts require separate models.
Paid-invoice funding, different event IDs for one invoice, fee/amount conservation, command dispatch, deletion owners and global liveness remain unmodeled here.
PGlite checks are real database regressions but do not establish the full PostgreSQL lock graph.
The model includes received/processing/applied/ignored transitions used by live platform handlers. Failed/quarantined administrative primitives require a separate model.

No fairness or temporal progress is assumed. Stuttering and indefinite provider/database failure are allowed; bounded safety does not establish eventual receipt delivery, eventual application or a real-time completion bound.

The 47-case conformance hook retains 41 receipt/publication checks and six command regressions, including expiry after provisional projection, rollback and response-loss replay. It is not a general refinement proof or a PostgreSQL lock-scheduling proof.
